THG-LJ.name: Leather Jug
THG-LJ.english: A jug shaped like a dressed figure
THG-LJ.medium: Leather; shaped to look like clothing
THG-LJ.fact: The museum describes a leather jug shaped like an Elizabethan woman. Its skirt has raised patterns; some leather types remain uncertain.
THG-LJ.limit: This is leather, not a textile. Neither the figure’s identity nor a British place of manufacture is established here. Confirm its record number and image use with the museum.
THG-LJ.credit: Image: Tudor House & Garden official website. Rights remain with the rights holders.

THG-GP.name: Bird Glass Panes
THG-GP.english: Decorated glass from the museum stores
THG-GP.fact: The museum suggests these bird-decorated panes may have come from the old Banqueting Hall windows.
THG-GP.limit: That origin is a suggestion, not a confirmed fact. Select one pane and confirm its record number. Glass is not a textile.
THG-GP.credit: Image: Tudor House & Garden official website. Rights remain with the rights holders.

GHT-MP.name: God’s House Tower by Moonlight
GHT-MP.status: Past loan exhibition; not owned by GHT
GHT-MP.fact: GHT records a Pether family loan display in 2019–2020. An opening report names this painting; its image record names Hampshire County Council as the collection.
GHT-MP.limit: Record FA1991.28 needs confirmation with the owner. Current display and image access are unconfirmed. The Art UK record itself could not be opened; see the linked image record and report.
GHT-MP.credit: Image: Hampshire County Council’s Fine Art Collection / Art UK; matched to the Commons record.

additional_sources.label: Image, title and record number: Commons / Art UK

GHT-EI.name: Everyone Involved: fabric wall hangings
GHT-EI.status: Shown at GHT in 2024; ownership not confirmed at GHT
GHT-EI.medium: Vintage and found fabric with painted images
GHT-EI.fact: The 2024 exhibition included fabric wall hangings. The venue announced a later move of the work to Southampton City Art Gallery.
GHT-EI.limit: Preferred textile option. Choose one hanging with the venue and artist. Past display does not establish GHT ownership or current access. A confirmed Chinese textile remains an open gap.
GHT-EI.credit: Image: God’s House Tower official website. Rights remain with the rights holders. Artwork: Ian Giles.

01.camera: Use the approved object photo by default. If the object is on display and photography is allowed, take one rear-camera photo, confirm the object, then crop a detail. Use a fixed fact card, not automatic object recognition. Return to the approved photo if the shot is blurred or reflects light.
01.camera_data: The proposed system sends only confirmed input. Record the input mode, failures and any help given. The atlas itself does not open a camera, call AI or collect visitor data.

adaptations.detail: The collar or raised skirt pattern.
adaptations.task: Ask about the gap between the clothing-like form and the leather material.
adaptations.question: What do you use to decide what this detail means?
adaptations.boundary: A photo cannot establish a leather type, date or maker’s intention.

adaptations.detail: One fabric edge or painted detail on one agreed wall hanging.
adaptations.task: Ask about what can be seen, then compare the reply with a checked record for that hanging.
adaptations.question: Do the material and its known story lead you to the same view?
adaptations.boundary: Use an approved digital image unless current access is confirmed; do not invent the fabric’s earlier owner.

01.case_note: Borrow close looking and source-based questions. A visitor-confirmed snapshot and a final personal note are additions in this proposal.

02.camera: Use a tablet or an overhead camera aimed at the work surface. Photograph only the visitor’s made shape. Preview, crop and confirm before sending one image. No continuous filming or body tracking is needed. If the camera fails, record that session as a text-only variant.
02.camera_data: The proposed system sends only confirmed input. Record the input mode, failures and any help given. The atlas itself does not open a camera, call AI or collect visitor data.

adaptations.detail: The collar’s folds, viewed in an approved detail photo.
adaptations.task: Make a loose shape using paper or ordinary cloth, then compare its form with the jug.
adaptations.question: What did making reveal that looking alone did not?
adaptations.boundary: This is a response to a leather form, not a textile replica or a test of historic craft skill.

adaptations.detail: The shapes made by fabric edges in one agreed wall hanging.
adaptations.task: Arrange or fold loose cloth into a new shape inspired by the detail; photograph it and describe its feel.
adaptations.question: Which part of the experience was missing from AI’s visual comparison?
adaptations.boundary: Use modern loose cloth, without tracing archive cartoons; do not claim the making repeats the artist’s process.

02.case_note: Borrow the link between physical making and camera input. Here AI compares once instead of producing a live stream, and the visitor explains what touch adds.

03.camera: Use an approved high-quality object image. A live camera would add changing light and angle without helping the question about local edits.
03.camera_data: The proposed system sends only confirmed input. Record the input mode, failures and any help given. The atlas itself does not open a camera, call AI or collect visitor data.

adaptations.detail: One small area of a single bird-decorated pane.
adaptations.task: Change one colour while keeping the bird’s outline and the rest of the image fixed.
adaptations.question: When does this become your new image rather than an account of the old object?
adaptations.boundary: The new image is not a restoration. Confirm image editing rights before implementation.

adaptations.detail: A small patch of sky or water in the Pether painting.
adaptations.task: Ask for one change while keeping the tower and all unmarked areas fixed.
adaptations.question: What must stay for the picture to keep its link to this place?
adaptations.boundary: Historical loan candidate; current access is unconfirmed. A painting is not a record of exactly how the site looked.

03.case_note: Borrow a visible change to an art image. Here the visitor marks a small area inside the image and states what must stay.

04.camera: Use the same approved object photo for both people. Text and discussion provide the evidence; a camera is not needed.
04.camera_data: The proposed system sends only confirmed input. Record the input mode, failures and any help given. The atlas itself does not open a camera, call AI or collect visitor data.

adaptations.detail: The whole jug, with its collar and skirt visible.
adaptations.task: Each visitor writes a line; compare both with the shared AI label.
adaptations.question: Did the shared words keep what mattered to each of you?
adaptations.boundary: Personal readings should remain distinct from sourced information about the object.

adaptations.detail: The same agreed wall hanging for both visitors.
adaptations.task: Each visitor writes about one visible feature or its documented context; then review the shared label.
adaptations.question: Did AI keep your different connections to the work?
adaptations.boundary: Do not ask visitors to disclose identities or treat them as speaking for a community.

04.case_note: Borrow a draft that people can review. Move the task to two visitors and preserve their separate words and disagreement.

05.camera: Use an approved photo, or take one rear-camera photo where allowed. The chosen image can stay on the device while only the message text goes to AI. Pass the tablet; no email, social account or external sending is required.
05.camera_data: The proposed system sends only confirmed input. Record the input mode, failures and any help given. The atlas itself does not open a camera, call AI or collect visitor data.

adaptations.detail: One bird or small painted detail on a selected pane.
adaptations.task: Choose it for a companion, write a message and compare the recipient’s reply with the intended meaning.
adaptations.question: Was the connection in the object, your words or your shared memory?
adaptations.boundary: A personal memory is the visitor’s account, not evidence about the glass.

adaptations.detail: One colour, fabric edge or painted detail from the agreed wall hanging.
adaptations.task: Choose a detail for someone you know; keep the original message beside the AI rewrite.
adaptations.question: Did the rewritten words still sound like the sender?
adaptations.boundary: No invented memory or personal identity; an approved digital image is the default.

05.case_note: Borrow choosing an object for another person. Add one optional AI rewrite and compare the sender’s meaning with the recipient’s response.
